messages:
support-jen: FYI AcmeCommerce is hitting a p99 jump (~8s) and a swarm of 429s for a subset of endpoints since ~00:30 UTC. They sent a few request_ids: r_8f3a, r_b12c, r_f00d. Logs attached in the ticket.

miguel: on it. are the 429s gateway rate limits or our internal throttles? any recent batcher config pushes for that tenant?

support-jen: customer says nothing changed on their side. We rolled a batching tweak to coalesce+linger at 00:15 for all tenants (CL #4217).

kevin: that matches timing. coalesce linger was increased from 6ms -> 40ms in the rollout. If traffic is bursty, that can create spike windows that look like a sudden burst to downstream rate limiters and also hold requests longer -> p99 tail.

naomi: quick check of logs: I see backend responses "429 rate_limited tenant=acme qps=120/100" interleaved with long wait times in batcher: "hold_window=40ms waited=3100ms" for tiny prompts. So a few tiny requests waited and then hit token TTL/rate windows.

miguel: reproducible locally? sara can you try a small script to replay tiny prompt pattern at low qps but bursty (1req every 4ms for short bursts) against staging with linger=40ms and hold drain?

sara: running now. command: ```for i in {1..200}; do curl -s -H "Authorization: Bearer test" -d '{"prompt":"hi"}' https://staging.api.redwood/v1/generate & sleep 0.004; done``` Will post results in 2m.

sara: repro: p95 ~200ms p99 ~6-9s when linger=40ms; when set linger=8ms p99 drops to ~250ms. Repro consistent.

kevin: so root is coalesce/linger tradeoff. Larger linger helps throughput for large prompts but for tiny prompts it creates batching tail where requests are queued and may be subject to tenant-level qps windows (billing/gateway) causing 429 cascade.

naomi: suggested mitigations: 1) rollback the global change for multi-tenant pools -> back to 6ms. 2) add tenant-aware short-linger override for small payloads (if request_size_tokens < 16 -> linger=6ms) 3) emergency: route Acme to dedicated pool or apply per-tenant throttle increase to avoid 429s.

miguel: agree. immediate action: rollback global linger now. I'll patch rollout to exclude multi-tenant pools and create a canary.

deploy-bot: deploy started: revert coalesce-linger-global (CL #4217-revert) by miguel. CI checks passed. ETA ~4m.

support-jen: letting Acme CS know: we rolled back to previous batching config and are monitoring.

sara: quick note for ops: small code snippet to set tenant-aware linger in runtime config: ```if (tokens <= 16 && tenant.multitenant) linger_ms = min(linger_ms, 8);``` Also add metric: batch_hold_wait_ms per-tenant to detect regressions.

kevin: follow-ups: (A) add e2e test that runs micro prompt burst profile on all build gates (B) add a metric alert for per-tenant 429-rate spike > 0.5% over baseline (C) document rollout runbook for coalesce/linger toggles.

naomi: created ticket INC-4321 and linked runbook + reproduction script. Assigning to kevin + miguel for next-day followup and naomi to monitor Acme for 24h.

miguel: monitoring: already see p99 back to normal on affected nodes. 429s dropped to baseline. marking hotfix as success, but we'll keep canary changes for a week. :thumbsup:
